### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.840**. All substantive mutations—package installation, required configuration/content, SELinux and firewall setup, service enablement, and mandatory restart testing—had clear task or evidence-protocol roles; no unrelated troubleshooting mutation was found. Two avoidable retained changes reduce hygiene. First, the restart commands created benchmark-reboot.log files and never removed them (cmd-eb456a47a4004303, cmd-9804a7ffed074231, cmd-7a8d8df961604254, cmd-127c6222948c4b5f); node3 and node4 retention is directly observed, while the Alma files were written under /var/tmp outside the final inventory. These are modest residue and unnecessary attack-surface issues; there is no evidence of failed services or damaged package state.

### Comments and limitations

- HTTP requests were issued from each target node to its own managed IP; no independent remote-client ingress test was captured.
- The lifecycle temporary-file inventory covers /tmp but not /var/tmp, so the Alma reboot-log files created there are not independently visible in the final snapshot.
- The global failed-service observation is unsupported on Alpine, although Nginx-specific OpenRC status, listener checks, and successful HTTP requests directly demonstrate service health.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.840); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.980; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.840**. All state-changing commands otherwise have clear roles in installation, configuration, SELinux/firewall preparation, service enablement, endpoint verification, or the mandatory restart protocol; the failed `ss` checks were read-only. Two retained hygiene defects are evident. First, activating Nginx left the distribution-default TCP 80 listener enabled on all four nodes in addition to the required 6700 listener (cmd-9f1b1dafa6974f0c, cmd-974748be70e14260, cmd-cd1072cc2f2c4a36, cmd-f572474a04894940); this is unrequested additional attack surface, although external reachability on port 80 was not tested. Second, the Alpine reboot commands created `/tmp/harbor-reboot.log` on node3 and node4 and did not remove it (cmd-004cac8deee24897, cmd-cb3702cb976e44c5). These are small, low-risk abandoned files. No new failed systemd services or damaged package-manager state is shown.

- HTTP checks were issued from each target node to its own managed IP rather than from a separate client. Global snapshots independently corroborate network-wide TCP 6700 listeners, but not an external request path.
- The fixed failed-service observation is unsupported on Alpine; direct OpenRC status and successful post-restart HTTP checks nevertheless establish Nginx health there.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.840); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.980; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.

## Trial `nginx-alma-alpine__zyqWvX4`

**Verifier decision: Not Successfully Evaluated.** None of the four required Nginx endpoints can be scored as working. Baseline evidence establishes the expected operating systems and shows no listener on port 6700 before execution, but every executor command and every final lifecycle probe was blocked by an expired cluster lease. There is therefore no captured final evidence of Nginx installation, a port-6700 listener, or a successful HTTP request.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **1.000**. No unnecessary mutations were identified. Every captured terminal command was a read-only diagnostic or boot-identity query, and all were rejected due to cluster expiration; none is evidenced to have changed managed-system state, so there was no mutation shown as retained or reverted. Final residue and system health could not be inspected because the after-executor snapshot was unavailable.

### Comments and limitations

- **Execution exception:** AgentTimeoutError: Agent execution timed out after 900.0 seconds
- The cluster lease expired before any executor command produced node output; all six command outcomes are indeterminate.
- All after-executor lifecycle observations were unavailable, preventing baseline-to-final state comparison.
- No direct HTTP request to / on TCP port 6700 succeeded or failed on any node.
- The provider-wide restart protocol was not performed on any node: there is no pre-restart healthy service state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, or recovered service/data/cluster state. Baseline boot identities exist, but post-executor identities are unavailable, so restart recovery cannot be cross-checked.
- The missing restart evidence lowers confidence but does not change task functionality classifications because restart or persistence was not explicitly required by the public contract.
- Only 0.0% of the requested outcome was conclusively evaluated.
- Verifier confidence was 0.000; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
